haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its output to the shadow store, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and 5,000+ invoices compared, with the gate met. A person promotes one step in the config service.
haiku-low.q4: The charge monitor, when charge failures exceed 2% in any 10-minute window. This applies in both or new_only, before day 35.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must go through shadow again, and the 7-day count restarts at zero.
haiku-low.q6: Once the flag has been new_only for 35 or more days. The document gives no explicit reason, though the usage log keeps only 35 days.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED for notification and for in-flight invoices at a change. Workers read billing_mode from the config service and keep their last known mode if it is unreachable.
haiku-low.q8: Nightly comparison results, stored with the shadow store and tagged by rollout epoch. Promotion is one step only and blocked during rollback. Enforcement before a gate is met is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: The charge monitor counts failed charges against attempts in every 10-minute window. Above 2%, it writes the rollback record, which starts the runner and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Charges falling due wait and are not dropped, since no new charge starts while the lock is set. They are made at handover, when the old engine charges each uncharged period once.
haiku-low.q11: The charge key (customer, billing period) is the unique ledger key and the provider idempotency key, so repeats are rejected. reconcile_ledger also adds ledger entries for provider charges that lack one.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in that step with charging paused and the flag unchanged. The step retries, since steps are idempotent, and on-call is paged if slow. A crashed rollback resumes from the recorded step.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store; it never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and 5000+ invoices compared (current rollout epoch only). A person promotes; nothing promotes itself.
sonnet.q4: A charge monitor: charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window. It applies in both and new_only, only before day 35. Not in shadow, where errors are only recorded.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must go through shadow again with fresh gates (7-day count starts at zero), then be promoted step by step.
sonnet.q6: After day 35: once the flag has been new_only for 35 or more days (new_only_committed, derived from the flag's change history), rollback requests are refused. The document gives the reason that the usage event log keeps only 35 days (open question 3), and says the old engine may be decommissioned.
sonnet.q7: Workers read the billing_mode flag (and the rollback record) from the config service, and keep their last known mode if it is unreachable. NOT STATED how they notice a change (no polling interval given). NOT STATED what happens to an invoice being processed at a mode change.
sonnet.q8: Nightly comparison results are stored with the shadow store, tagged with a rollout epoch; only current-epoch results count. The flag's change history gives time in mode (14-day gate). The nightly job notifies owners when a gate is met. NOT STATED that anything technically blocks a premature promotion; promotion is a person's action under the gate condition, though skipping steps is not allowed and promotion is blocked during a rollback.
sonnet.q9: The charge monitor. It counts failed charges against attempts in each 10-minute window. When the failure rate is above 2%, it writes the rollback record (lock, origin mode, current step pause_charging, start time), which starts the rollback runner; on-call is paged. It is ignored if a rollback is already running.
sonnet.q10: Charges that fall due wait and are not dropped, because the lock is set and no new charge starts. They are made at handover, after billing_mode is set to old_only and the lock released, when the old engine charges every period with no charged ledger entry, once.
sonnet.q11: The charge key (customer, billing_period) is a unique ledger key and the provider's idempotency key, so a repeat is rejected. Also reconcile_ledger adds provider charges missing from the ledger as charged, and reprocessing and handover only handle periods with no charged ledger entry.
sonnet.q12: The rollback stays in that step and retries (steps are idempotent). Charging stays paused, the flag is unchanged (still origin mode), and on-call is paged if it takes too long. It never skips a step. A crashed rollback resumes from the recorded step in the rollback record.
